title: A timeout wrapper
description:
Give any promise a time limit.

```
withTimeout(sleep(50, "fast"), 100)   -> "fast"
withTimeout(sleep(500, "slow"), 100)  -> rejects: TimeoutError: took longer than 100 ms
```
hints: Make a second promise that rejects after `ms`, and race the two: `Promise.race([promise, timer])`.
Keep the id from `setTimeout` and call `clearTimeout(id)` in a `.finally()` on the race.
requirements: `withTimeout(promise, ms)` resolves or rejects like `promise`, unless `ms` passes first; then it rejects with a `TimeoutError` (your own class).
Clear the timer when the promise finishes first, so the program does not wait for it.
stretch: Write `retry(fn, times, ms)` that calls `fn()` again when it times out, up to `times` attempts.
